title: Complementary FET (CFET) 3D transistor manufacturability
bottleneck: CFET stacks n-type and p-type transistors vertically to continue area scaling, but it requires sequential or monolithic 3D processing: wafer bonding or layer transfer, top-device thermal budgets that don't destroy bottom devices, and interconnect routing through the stacked structure. No fab has demonstrated CFET at high volume, and thermal-budget conflicts between stacked layers are a fundamental integration headache.
why_it_blocks: CFET is the industry's planned answer to the end of lateral transistor scaling; without it, density gains after 2nm-class nodes slow sharply, forcing expensive reliance on 3D packaging alone to keep performance-per-dollar growing.
current_state: Research consortia (notably imec) have demonstrated CFET device prototypes and process flows, and foundries list it on roadmaps for late-2020s/early-2030s nodes. Manufacturing-worthy flows with acceptable yield are not yet proven.
